content.value_statement: System issues and shell scripts often require careful, repeatable triage across several operating systems. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for diagnosis, scripting, testing, and automation.
actual_capabilities: Lists phased workflows for environment assessment, script analysis, debugging, development, testing, troubleshooting, and automation.
Names companion skills for Bash patterns, ShellCheck, Bats testing, DevOps troubleshooting, incident response, and workflow automation.
Provides example diagnostic commands for system resources, logs, networking, processes, disk usage, and service failures.
Includes a defensive Bash script template with logging, option parsing, error handling, and help output.
Shows Bats test examples and quality gates for scripts before completion.
limitations: It is a workflow guide, not an executable tool or command runner.
Commands must be reviewed for the target system before use.
Some examples need administrative privileges or package managers that may not exist.
It does not replace platform documentation, change control, or incident response policy.

use_cases.title: Triage Linux server issues
use_cases.description: Follow a clear sequence for checking resources, logs, networking, processes, disks, and service state.

use_cases.title: Improve shell scripts
use_cases.description: Review script structure, add safer error handling, lint with ShellCheck, and plan focused Bats tests.

use_cases.title: Plan recurring maintenance
use_cases.description: Design scheduled maintenance tasks with monitoring, quality gates, and review steps before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a basic script failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner troubleshooting for a failing shell script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me diagnose a shell script failure. Ask for the script, error output, operating system, and expected behavior before suggesting fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Bash script for release
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate script review before production use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Bash script for quoting, error handling, logging, option parsing, ShellCheck findings, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a server incident
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operating system troubleshooting during an outage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a cautious incident triage plan for a server outage. Separate observation steps, risky actions, rollback options, and escalation points.

prompt_templates.title: Design automated maintenance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation planning for recurring administration tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a recurring maintenance workflow. Include prerequisites, safety checks, tests, monitoring, scheduling options, and operator approval points.

output_examples.input: I need to troubleshoot high CPU usage on a Linux server.
output_examples.output: The response would organize checks for active processes, load, logs, and recent changes, then suggest cautious next actions.

output_examples.input: I have a Bash script that exits unpredictably.
output_examples.output: The response would review error handling, variable quoting, debug tracing, ShellCheck results, and small tests for failing branches.

output_examples.input: I want weekly log cleanup automation.
output_examples.output: The response would outline scheduling choices, retention rules, dry-run checks, monitoring, and review steps before enabling automation.

best_practices: Share the operating system, shell, script excerpt, error output, and expected result.
Ask for observation steps before requesting commands that change system state.
Review any command that uses sudo, cron, service management, or root filesystem scans.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated commands on production systems without review.
Do not skip ShellCheck, tests, or rollback planning for automation.
Do not treat placeholder hosts, paths, services, or scripts as deployment-ready values.

faq.question: Does this skill run operating system commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. A user or agent must still choose and run any command.

faq.question: Which operating systems does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Linux, macOS, and Windows workflows, with many examples focused on Unix-style shells.

faq.question: Can it help write production Bash scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes structure, logging, option parsing, error handling, testing, and quality gate guidance.

faq.question: Can it diagnose server incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a phased triage approach for resources, logs, networking, processes, disks, and services.

faq.question: Does it replace ShellCheck or Bats?
faq.answer: No. It tells the assistant when to use those tools and how to interpret their role in the workflow.

faq.question: What should users review most carefully?
faq.answer: Users should review commands that use elevated privileges, scheduled tasks, service changes, or broad filesystem searches.
